advances: Ordinary planar uniform area, arbitrary convex boundaries and explicit local affine radius. Controls the total missing area of the constructed triangle, with cap distance bounded above by that area fraction.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Work in the normalized frame and write $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)$. If $\delta=0$, take $S=Q=T$ and its centroid. The low-cap localization lemma reduces caps below its threshold to the one-vertex case, where AM–GM gives at least $4(1/3)^2$; higher caps exceed $4/9$. Otherwise Hausdorff comparison gives
$$
\{x,y\ge\delta,\ x+y\le1-2\delta\}\subseteq Q
\subseteq\{x,y\ge-\delta,\ x+y\le1+2\delta\}.
$$
The outer inclusion follows directly by distance; for the inner one, adding $[-\delta,\delta]^2$ to the indicated inner triangle stays in $T$, while $h_Q(u)\ge h_T(u)-\delta\lVert u\rVert_1$ for each support direction $u$.

Choose the leftmost point on $y=1/2$, the bottommost point on $x=1/2$, and the last point on $x=y$. The inclusions give these as $w_1=(\theta_1,1/2)$, $w_2=(1/2,\theta_2)$, and $w_0=(1/2+\theta_0,1/2+\theta_0)$ with $|\theta_i|\le\delta$. Their supporting lines, with the sides containing $Q$, can be written
$$
x\ge c_1+b_1y,\qquad y\ge c_2+b_2x,\qquad
(1-k)x+(1+k)y\le1+2\theta_0
$$
with $|b_1|,|b_2|,|k|\le8\delta$ and $|c_1|,|c_2|\le5\delta$. Indeed the inner points $(\delta,1/4),(\delta,3/4)$ exclude a horizontal first support and bound its slope by $4(\delta-\theta_1)$; points to the right on $y=1/2$ give its orientation. The bound on the intercept follows from $c_1=\theta_1-b_1/2$, and the second support is obtained by interchanging coordinates. For the top support the inner points $(3/4-\delta,1/4-\delta)$ and its swap have sum $1-2\delta$ and difference $\pm1/2$. Thus the coefficient of the sum is nonzero and normalized to $1$, with the retained side oriented by the points below $w_0$ on the diagonal; $|k|\le4(\delta+\theta_0)$.

The first two halfplanes form a cone translated to their intersection, with generators $(1,b_2),(b_1,1)$; the top functional on either generator is at least $1-16\delta-64\delta^2>0$. Hence their intersection is a bounded triangle $S\supseteq Q$. Label its vertices $a_0,a_1,a_2$ near $0,e_1,e_2$. At $a_0$ the two coordinate bounds are $(5\delta+40\delta^2)/(1-64\delta^2)\le6\delta$. For $a_1$, eliminating $y$ between the second and third lines gives an $x$ numerator within $8\delta$ of $1$ and a denominator within $17\delta$ of $1$, so $|x-1|\le26\delta$ and $|y|\le14\delta$. The other vertex has the swapped bounds. Thus $\lVert a_i-e_i\rVert_\infty\le30\delta$ for $i=1,2$. Let $M=(a_1-a_0,a_2-a_0)$. Its entries differ from those of the identity by at most $36\delta$, giving $\lVert M^{-1}\rVert_\infty\le(1-72\delta)^{-1}$. In the frame $x\mapsto M^{-1}(x-a_0)$ each $w_i$ is on its corresponding edge of $T$ within $43\delta/(1-72\delta)\le44\delta$ of the midpoint: before multiplying by $M^{-1}$ the errors are at most $\delta$, $6\delta$, and $36\delta$ from the point, translation and matrix, respectively (standard midpoints have $\ell_1$ norm at most one). In particular each is strictly inside its edge. The inner triangle gives $|Q|\ge(1-4\delta)^2/2$, and expanding $\det M$ gives $|S|\le(1+72\delta+2592\delta^2)/2$. Hence
$$
\tau\le\frac{80\delta+2576\delta^2}{1+72\delta+2592\delta^2}\le81\delta<1/10000.
$$

In barycentrics $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ of $S$, the missing set $S\setminus Q$ is exactly the union of strict exterior support caps $\{x\in S:a\cdot x>h_Q(a)\}$, over nonzero $a$. A nonempty strict cap excludes some vertex $i$ strictly. The other two vertices are strictly retained: otherwise the retained interior contact on an incident edge would be strictly excluded. Thus each strict cap is of the form $\lambda_j/b_j+\lambda_k/b_k<1$ with $b_j,b_k>0$ and each intercept at most $1/2+44\delta<B=501/1000$ by those edge contacts. Its fraction $b_jb_k$ is at most $\tau$, so at least one intercept is below $1/100$. Call such a coordinate short. Let $R_i$ be the union of strict caps excluding vertex $i$, and $O_{i,k}$ the union among these whose coordinate toward the remaining vertex $j$ is short, so $k$ is the possibly long coordinate. These unions are relatively open and Borel, and $R_i$ is the union of its two orientation classes.

The $R_i$ are disjoint. For different $i,j$ use their common edge contact with barycentrics $\lambda_j=t$, $\lambda_i=1-t$. A point in $R_i$ satisfies $\lambda_j<t(1-\lambda_k/B)$ by its witnessing cap and the two intercept bounds; a point in $R_j$ satisfies $\lambda_i<(1-t)(1-\lambda_k/B)$. The sum of both strict inequalities contradicts $\lambda_i+\lambda_j=1-\lambda_k$ since $B<1$. Thus with $\tau_i=|R_i|/|S|$ one has $\sum_i\tau_i=\tau$.

For a through-mark cap of $S$ of fraction at most $4/9+1/10000$, when the mark has barycentric deviations at most $1/10000$, the low-cap localization lemma gives a vertex type with two coefficients in $(29/20,31/20)$. A low cap at $j$ misses $O_{i,k}$, because its left side on that set is at least $(29/20)(1-\lambda_j)>1$. A low cap at $k$ can meet $O_{i,k}$ only where
$$
\lambda_k\ge 1-1/A_i+(A_j/A_i-1)\lambda_j
\ge9/29-1/1550>309/1000,
$$
using the coefficient window and $\lambda_j\le1/100$. In the barycentric coordinates $(\lambda_j,\lambda_k)$ the union-tail lemma bounds this intersection by $(3/20)|O_{i,k}|$; the fixed area Jacobian cancels. A low cap at $i$ may meet all of $R_i$. Therefore every low cap of vertex type $i$ loses at most $L_i|S|$, where
$$
L_i=\tau_i+\frac3{20}\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{|O_{j,i}|}{|S|},\qquad
0\le L_i\le\tau,\qquad \sum_i L_i\le13\tau/10 .
$$
These bounds count own-vertex union mass once and at most two orientation unions per other vertex. A cap at the short neighbor misses that orientation even if the two orientations overlap.

Put $\bar L=\sum_i L_i/3$ and choose $y$ by $\lambda_i(y)=1/3+(3/4)(\bar L-L_i)$. These coordinates sum to one, have deviations at most $3\tau/4$, and give a neighborhood inside $S$ with all coordinates greater than $1/100$. This neighborhood misses every exterior cap, so $y\in\operatorname{int}Q$. For any low cap of type $i$ through $y$, AM–GM and its equation at $y$ give original area fraction at least $4\lambda_j(y)\lambda_k(y)$. Writing $\Delta_i=\lambda_i(y)-1/3$, the retained fraction relative to $|S|$ is at least
$$
4\lambda_j(y)\lambda_k(y)-L_i
=4/9-\bar L+4\Delta_j\Delta_k
\ge4/9-13\tau/30-9\tau^2/4 .
$$
Every other cap through $y$ started above $4/9+1/10000$ and loses at most $\tau$, so also meets this bound. A containing halfspace contains the parallel cap tightened to $y$. Divide by $1-\tau$ and subtract $4/9$ to get the first depth estimate. Its difference from $\tau/180$ is $\tau(1-404\tau)/[180(1-\tau)]\ge0$. If $\tau=0$ the full-dimensional nested bodies are equal and the same proof gives the centroid estimate. The signed uniform-density difference has negative part supported on $S\setminus Q$ of mass $\tau$, proving the total variation identity and the cap-distance upper bound. Invertible affine transport preserves all these normalized quantities.
statement:
Let $Q$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body in $\mathbb R^2$ and suppose that some invertible affine map $A$ makes $\delta=d_{H,\infty}(AQ,\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2))\le10^{-6}$. There is a triangle $S\supseteq Q$ constructed from three supporting lines, with $\tau=1-|Q|/|S|\le81\delta$, such that its normalized maximal ordinary halfspace depth satisfies
$$
D(Q)-4/9\ge\frac{\tau/90-9\tau^2/4}{1-\tau}\ge\tau/180.
$$
The uniform probability measures obey $d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_S)\le\operatorname{TV}(\mu_Q,\mu_S)=\tau$, where cap distance is the supremum of the absolute probability difference over closed halfspaces and total variation is the supremum over measurable sets. In particular $\inf_{S'}d_{\rm cap}(\mu_Q,\mu_{S'})\le180[D(Q)-4/9]$ over full-dimensional triangles.
title: Explicit enclosing-triangle stability for an arbitrary near-triangle planar convex body
